claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child or children.

**First, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for:**

To determine eligibility, I need to understand your child's age. Could you please tell me:

1. **How many children are you inquiring about?**
2. **For each child, what is their current age or date of birth?**

This will help me determine which path through the eligibility check applies to your situation. Remember, for Child Benefit, the general rule is that children must be:
- **Under 16**, OR
- **16-19 and in education or approved training**, OR
- Other specific circumstances

What information can you share about your child/children?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old and lives with me at home. Just the one child I'm inquiring about.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So I'm helping you with eligibility for your son **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, he meets the basic age requirement for Child Benefit. Now let me continue with the next checks to determine your full eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Since Alex is 8 years old, I assume he's not in paid employment, but I need to confirm this for our assessment.

Is Alex:
- Not in any paid work, OR
- Working less than 24 hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 8! He just goes to school like any other kid his age.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! That's what I expected for an 8-year-old. Alex is not in paid work, so he meets this requirement.

Let me move forward with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, is Alex:
- **Not** receiving Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) in his own name, AND
- **Not** receiving Universal Credit as a benefit claimant in his own right?

(In other words, any benefits he receives would be as part of your household claim, not in his own name?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't get any benefits in his own name. He's just a child, so any benefits would be through me as the parent.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the expected situation for an 8-year-old. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old and still at primary school, I assume he's not in any apprenticeship at all. Can you confirm:

- Is Alex **not in any apprenticeship program** (which would be the case for a typical 8-year-old)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's definitely not in an apprenticeship - he's only 8! He's just in primary school doing normal school work.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - Alex is not in any apprenticeship. Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

This is an important check. Child Benefit requires the claimant to meet certain residency criteria. Let me ask about your situation:

**Which of the following applies to you:**

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (This is the most common situation)

2. Or do you have a more complex residency situation, such as:
   - Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Living abroad as a Crown servant?
   - Something else?

What's your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - we're based in Manchester. Nothing complicated, just a regular UK resident.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward. You meet the residency requirement as you normally live in the UK. Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

You mentioned that Alex lives with you at home, so let me confirm:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and upkeep?** This means:
- You **live with him** (which you've already said), OR
- You **contribute to his upkeep** (food, clothes, housing, etc.), OR
- You're making **maintenance payments** under a court order or agreement

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like you're living with Alex and supporting him - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives with me and I take care of him. I provide everything he needs - food, clothes, housing, all of it.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - you're responsible for Alex's care and upkeep. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

This is an important check because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any given time.

Can you confirm:
- **Is Alex's other parent, or anyone else, currently claiming Child Benefit for him?**
- Or **are you the only person claiming for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm the only one who would be claiming for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear - you're the only claimant for Alex. Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Where is Alex living currently?**

I need to check if any special circumstances apply to his living situation:

- **Is Alex living normally at home with you?**
- Or is he:
  - Currently in hospital?
  - In local authority care?
  - Fostered with another family?

What's Alex's current living situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex is actually in local authority care at the moment, but he comes home to stay with me every weekend. So he's not there full-time - he still spends quite a bit of time at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex is in local authority care but still spends weekends with you at home. This is an important factor in the eligibility assessment.

Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: This is important for your eligibility - I need to understand the duration and frequency of Alex's time in care.**

There are two key scenarios that would allow you to continue claiming Child Benefit:

1. **Has Alex been in care for 8 weeks or less?** (If so, you can still claim during this period)

OR

2. **Does Alex spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you?** (Even if he's been in care longer than 8 weeks, you can still claim if he spends this much time at home)

Can you tell me:
- **How long has Alex been in local authority care?**
- **How much time does he spend at home with you each week?** (For example, just weekends, or weekends plus other days?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been in care for a couple of months now, so it's more than 8 weeks. But yes, he does spend quite a bit of time at home with me - he comes home every weekend, so that's definitely more than 24 hours a week that he's with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! This is good news. Even though Alex has been in care for more than 8 weeks, he spends more than 24 hours per week at home with you (every weekend plus potentially other time), which means you can continue to claim Child Benefit for him.

Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

This is the last eligibility check. I need to confirm:

- **Is the local council paying for Alex's care, accommodation, or maintenance while he's in care?**

Or to put it another way:
- **Are you responsible for paying towards Alex's upkeep while he's in local authority care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the local council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. I'm the one responsible for his upkeep - I still provide for him when he's home on weekends and I cover his needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's the final piece of information I need. You've met all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarize your situation and provide you with the outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex.**

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

**Child:** Alex (8 years old)  
**Status:** ✅ ELIGIBLE

### Why You're Eligible:

Despite Alex being in local authority care, you meet all the eligibility criteria:

1. ✅ Alex is under 16 (qualifying age)
2. ✅ He's not working full-time and is in primary school
3. ✅ He doesn't receive benefits in his own right
4. ✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
5. ✅ You're responsible for his care and upkeep
6. ✅ You're the only person claiming for him
7. ✅ **Key factor:** Alex spends more than 24 hours per week at home with you (every weekend), which keeps him eligible under the special provisions for children in care
8. ✅ The local council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance

### Important Information:

The fact that Alex spends regular time at home with you every weekend is crucial to your eligibility. As long as he continues to spend at least 24 hours per week with you, you can continue to claim Child Benefit, even though he's in local authority care.

### Next Steps:

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through:
- **Online:** www.gov.uk/apply-child-benefit
- **By phone:** 0300 200 3100

For more information about Child Benefit, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your eligibility?

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) He is under 16 years old, which makes him a qualifying child; (2) He is not working full-time and is in primary school; (3) He is not receiving benefits in his own right; (4) He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (5) You normally live in the UK (Manchester), meeting residency requirements; (6) You are responsible for Alex's care and upkeep, providing food, clothes, housing, and other necessities; (7) You are the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex; (8) Although Alex is currently in local authority care, he spends more than 24 hours per week at home with you (every weekend), which qualifies him under the special care provisions; (9) The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance - you remain responsible for his upkeep.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible for Child Benefit for your son Alex. Despite him being in local authority care, the key factor in your favour is that he spends regular and substantial time at home with you (every weekend, which exceeds the 24 hours per week threshold). You also remain financially responsible for his upkeep, and the local council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance. This means you can continue to claim Child Benefit for Alex while he remains in this care arrangement."
